I make my own health care products because it is way cheaper and you know exactly what you're putting on your body. I've been doing this for about 4 years now so these are my collections of recipes from experimenting and researching.

For shaving: I've been using an double edged (de) safety razor with blades that I got in bulk for about $0.02 each, with Williams mug shaving soap. I probably spent about $60 on the razor, blades, soap, and a shaving brush about 5 years ago. I still have tons of blades left and it's just about time to buy more soap, which is only a couple bucks a bar and it lasts over a year.

For shampoo: I use soapnuts with essential oils. The soapnuts are berries that are native to the Himalayan region. The berries have saponin in them that acts as a cleansing agent. To make the soapnuts liquid to use as soap or shampoo, simply put about 12 soapnuts in water to a pot and reduce the liquid by 1/3. So 6 cups water reduced down to 4 cups soapnut liquid. They don't produce suds, so you might not feel like you're getting clean compared to normal shampoo, but together with the essential oils your hair will be clean and smell great. For the essential oils make sure they say "essential oil" not "fragrance oil" because fragrance oils are synthetic and you won't get the cleaning effects of the actual essential oil. For the shampoo I use tea tree oil, lemongrass oil, rosemary oil, aragon oil, and lime oil. You can experiment with the essential oils, but make sure to look up their properties so you know why you're using a particular oil. For example, in my shampoo the lime essential oil acts as a bactericidal and a disinfectant to clean you hair. List of essential oil properties. For 8oz of liquid soapnuts I use about 45 drops of essential oils TOTAL.

For soap: I also use liquid soapnuts with essential oils, just because I really haven't got into making homemade bar soap. I use tee tree oil, oregano oil, lavender oil, lemongrass oil, lime oil, and eucalytpus oil. For 8oz of liquid soapnuts I use about 30 drops of essential oils TOTAL.

For deodorant: I mix equal parts arrowroot powder, baking soda, and fractionated coconut oil(stays liquid) and add in bergamont oil, tea tree oil, cinnamon oil, and grapefruit oil. For 3 tablespoons of of the main ingredients(1 TB each) I use 12 drops of essential oils. I recommend making this small batch at first and see how your armpits feel, if they feel irritated, next batch use less baking soda and more arrowroot powder till it doesn't feel irritated.

If you're used to using the other kind of store bought deodorant that builds up all the aluminum and/or titanium or whatever you will smell terrible if you just start using this right away. So first, you will need to use a paste of bentonite clay and water and let it sit for 20 mins, then rub it under your armpits and let it dry there. Once it drys it will start to feel irritated, that is when you jump in the shower and wash it off. Now, the combination of the bentonite clay and water will give the paste a strong negative charge, and the toxins in your armpits have a positive charge, so they will be attracted and pulled out by the paste. So make sure that you DO NOT use METAL when touching the bentonite clay at all as this will negate the effect. Also, look up the Jarisch–Herxheimer reaction as you might experience this and this could put you off from continuing, or make you think that the paste is making you sick. I recommend doing this paste for 2-3 days in a row, preferably when you have a few days off from work. You don't want to use deodorant when doing this paste because your armpits will be red and irritated if you use the deodorant. When you're done with the 2-3 days of detox, you can use the new deodorant and just dab a little on each armpit.

For kitchen de-greaser: Mix 1 cup hot water with 1 tablespoon baking soda, now SLOWLY mix in 1 cup distilled vinegar. I say slowly because the baking soda with the vinegar will expand and bubble over very quickly(if you've ever made a volcano science experiment you know what I mean). Finally, add in 4 drops of orange oil. Now put this in a spray bottle and use on tough to get out grease on grills, stovetops, etc. Make sure to spray it on and let it sit for a couple mins to let it work. Just don't use on grout as the mixture will eat it up.

All-purpose counter-top cleaner: Mix 1 teaspoon borax, 1/2 teaspoon washing powder(if you don't have it, how to make: bake baking soda at 400F for about an hour till the baking soda is no longer shiny, but looks dull), 1 TB liquid soapnuts or regular dish soap, 4 drops lemon essential oil, 4 drops lavendar oil, 10 drops orange oil, and 2 cups water. Put in a spray bottle and shake and it's ready to clean messes from countertops.

Grout cleaner: Mix baking soda with hydrogen peroxide into a paste. Put on grout and wait a few mins and then scrub.

Scrubbing powder: Mix together equal parts sea salt, borax, and baking soda. Apply to your bathtub with a scouring pad and a tiny bit of water and your tub will shine.
